name: Scientific computing toolkit powers numerical relativity
summary: Numerical relativity is a flagship application of large-scale scientific computing: adaptive mesh refinement, high-order finite-difference and multidomain spectral solvers, constraint damping and parallel HPC turned the Einstein equations into working codes, culminating in the 2005 binary-black-hole breakthrough.
sources: Pretorius (2005). "Evolution of Binary Black-Hole Spacetimes". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 121101. [arXiv:gr-qc/0507014](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0507014)

name: Well-posed hyperbolic formulations and PDE integrators
summary: The Einstein equations become a stable initial-value problem only in strongly hyperbolic formulations (generalized harmonic, BSSN with moving punctures); they are then evolved by method-of-lines Runge–Kutta with finite differences plus AMR or spectral methods, with constraint damping controlling constraint growth.
sources: Pretorius (2005). "Evolution of Binary Black-Hole Spacetimes". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 121101. [arXiv:gr-qc/0507014](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0507014)

name: GR as a showcase of mathematical-physics methods
summary: GR brings many mathematical methods together: the Einstein equations as a constrained nonlinear hyperbolic PDE system, Green's-function solutions of linearized gravity, perturbation expansions (post-Newtonian, black-hole perturbation theory) and spin-weighted spherical harmonics for radiation.
sources: Einstein (1916). "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie". *Ann. Phys.* 354, 769. [doi:10.1002/andp.19163540702](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19163540702)

name: Lorentzian geometry is the language of gravity
summary: GR models gravity as curvature of a Lorentzian manifold: free fall is geodesic motion, the equivalence principle is local flatness in normal coordinates, and tidal forces are the Riemann tensor acting through geodesic deviation.
sources: Einstein (1916). "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie". *Ann. Phys.* 354, 769. [doi:10.1002/andp.19163540702](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19163540702)

name: Contracted Bianchi identity fixes the Einstein tensor
summary: The contracted Bianchi identity makes the Einstein tensor identically divergence-free, so it can consistently be set equal to a conserved stress–energy tensor; the field equations are a statement in Riemannian geometry about Ricci curvature.

name: Diffeomorphism invariance gives local conservation
summary: Diffeomorphism invariance of the matter action implies covariant conservation of the stress–energy tensor, and invariance of the Einstein–Hilbert action implies the Bianchi identity (Noether's second theorem); globally conserved energy exists only with Killing vectors or asymptotic symmetries.
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)

name: Planck scale marks where quantum gravity is order one
summary: Combining G, ħ and c gives the Planck length, time and energy, where gravitational and quantum effects are both order one; every quantum-gravity programme is organized around this scale, and its ~10^15 gap above LHC energies is why direct tests are so hard.

name: Matched filtering and Bayesian inference of GW signals
summary: GW detection is a likelihood-ratio test built on a noise-weighted inner product (matched filtering against template banks); significance comes from time-slide background estimation, and source parameters from Bayesian posteriors.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Special relativity is Poincaré invariance
summary: Special relativity says physics is invariant under the Poincaré group; Wigner's unitary irreducible representations classify particles by mass and spin, and the double cover SL(2,C) of the Lorentz group gives spinors.
map: SO^+(1,3)\cong SL(2,\mathbb C)/\mathbb Z_2,\quad P^\mu P_\mu=-m^2c^2\ (\text{Casimir})
sources: Wigner (1939). "On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group". *Ann. Math.* 40, 149. [doi:10.2307/1968551](https://doi.org/10.2307/1968551)

name: Lorentz transformations as isometries of Minkowski metric
summary: Minkowski's reformulation makes Lorentz transformations the isometries of a flat metric of Lorentzian signature; four-vectors and tensors make laws manifestly covariant, and GR reuses the same machinery for curved metrics.
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Ann. Phys.* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)

name: CPT tests double as Lorentz-invariance tests
summary: The CPT theorem follows from Lorentz invariance plus locality, and in local interacting QFT CPT violation implies Lorentz violation; so kaon mass differences, antihydrogen spectroscopy and Penning-trap particle–antiparticle comparisons constrain Lorentz-violating coefficients of the Standard-Model Extension.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: Retarded Green's function yields the quadrupole formula
summary: In Lorenz gauge, linearized gravity is a sourced wave equation for the trace-reversed perturbation; the same retarded Green's function as in electrodynamics gives the far-zone field and hence the quadrupole formula for gravitational radiation.
sources: Blanchet (2014; updated 2024). "Post-Newtonian Theory for Gravitational Waves". *Living Rev. Relativ.* [arXiv:1310.1528](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.1528)

name: Ringdown quasinormal modes as Green's-function poles
summary: Black-hole ringdown is a sum of quasinormal modes: complex frequencies at the poles of the perturbation Green's function in the lower half ω-plane (plus a branch cut that gives late-time tails), computed by Leaver's continued fractions or WKB; they depend only on mass and spin, which enables black-hole spectroscopy.

name: Euclidean periodicity fixes the Hawking temperature
summary: Wick-rotating the Schwarzschild metric gives a smooth Euclidean geometry only if imaginary time is periodic with period 2πc/κ; since thermal Green's functions are periodic in imaginary time (KMS condition), that period is ħ/k_BT, which is the Hawking temperature (Gibbons–Hawking).
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: String worldsheets as Riemann surfaces
summary: Perturbative string amplitudes are integrals over moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces; worldsheet conformal invariance makes the theory a 2D CFT, worked with holomorphic functions, contour-integral operator product expansions and modular invariance of the torus amplitude.

name: Template-bank metric on the waveform manifold
summary: The fractional SNR lost between neighbouring templates defines a Riemannian metric on source-parameter space, and template banks are lattices laid out with this metric; the related Fisher information matrix gives forecast parameter uncertainties.

name: Petrov classification and algebraically special metrics
summary: Classifying the Weyl tensor by its principal null directions (Petrov types, Newman–Penrose formalism) organizes the exact solutions; Kerr found the rotating black hole by searching for algebraically special vacuum metrics, and the Goldberg–Sachs theorem links that degeneracy to shear-free null congruences.
sources: Kerr (1963). "Gravitational Field of a Spinning Mass as an Example of Algebraically Special Metrics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 11, 237. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237)

name: Singularity theorems and global causal structure
summary: Global Lorentzian geometry (the Raychaudhuri focusing equation, trapped surfaces, conformal compactification into Penrose diagrams) proves that a trapped surface plus an energy condition implies geodesic incompleteness, so black-hole singularities are generic rather than artifacts of symmetry.
sources: Penrose (1965). "Gravitational Collapse and Space-Time Singularities". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 14, 57. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.14.57](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.14.57)

name: Ashtekar connection variables recast GR as gauge theory
summary: Rewriting canonical GR with an SU(2) connection and a densitized triad (Ashtekar, later Ashtekar–Barbero) gives it a Yang–Mills-like phase space; holonomies of the connection and fluxes of the triad are the basic variables quantized in loop quantum gravity.
sources: Ashtekar (1986). "New Variables for Classical and Quantum Gravity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 57, 2244. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.2244](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.2244)

name: Lovelock's theorem defines the routes to modified gravity
summary: In four dimensions the only symmetric, divergence-free rank-2 tensor built from the metric and its first two derivatives is a combination of G_μν and g_μν; every modified-gravity theory escapes this by adding fields (scalar-tensor, Horndeski), higher derivatives (f(R)), extra dimensions or nonlocality.

name: Random-subsystem entropy gives the Page curve
summary: Averaging subsystem entanglement entropy over Haar-random pure states in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space gives nearly maximal entropy for the smaller factor; applied to a black hole plus its radiation, this gives the Page curve (radiation entropy rises, then falls after the Page time), which unitarity requires and Hawking's calculation misses.
sources: Page (1993). "Information in black hole radiation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 3743. [arXiv:hep-th/9306083](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9306083)
Penington (2020). "Entanglement wedge reconstruction and the information paradox". *JHEP* 09, 002. [arXiv:1905.08255](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08255)

name: SU(2) spin networks and the quantized area spectrum
summary: LQG states are spin networks, graphs whose edges carry SU(2) irreducible representations j and whose nodes carry intertwiners; the area operator is diagonal on them with eigenvalues fixed by the SU(2) Casimir, so area is discrete.
sources: Rovelli & Smolin (1995). "Discreteness of area and volume in quantum gravity". *Nucl. Phys. B* 442, 593. [arXiv:gr-qc/9411005](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9411005)

name: AdS isometries equal the boundary conformal group
summary: The isometry group of AdS_{d+1} is SO(d,2), exactly the conformal group of d-dimensional Minkowski space (extended to PSU(2,2|4) for AdS5×S5 and N=4 SYM); this symmetry match underlies the bulk-field/boundary-operator dictionary, where bulk mass fixes the operator's scaling dimension.
sources: Maldacena (1998). "The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 231. [arXiv:hep-th/9711200](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9711200)
Witten (1998). "Anti De Sitter Space And Holography". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 253. [arXiv:hep-th/9802150](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9802150)

name: Killing symmetries give conserved orbital constants
summary: Each Killing vector of a black-hole metric gives a quantity conserved along geodesics (energy from ∂_t, angular momentum from ∂_φ), and Komar integrals define mass and spin; Kerr also has a Killing tensor that gives the Carter constant, a hidden symmetry that makes geodesic motion integrable.

name: No local gravitational energy; GW energy as averaged or boundary charge
summary: Because diffeomorphisms are a local gauge symmetry, Noether's second theorem gives no gauge-invariant local energy density for gravity; GW energy is defined only by averaging over wavelengths (Isaacson tensor) or as charges at null infinity, where the Bondi mass decreases as waves escape and BMS supertranslation charges are tied to the gravitational memory effect.
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)

name: Spontaneous Lorentz violation in the SME
summary: Lorentz symmetry could break spontaneously, with a vector or tensor field acquiring a vacuum expectation value that picks out a frame (Kostelecký–Samuel, bumblebee models); the Standard-Model Extension parametrizes the resulting background coefficients, and the associated Nambu–Goldstone modes have been proposed as photons or gravitons.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: Black-hole entropy is horizon area in Planck units
summary: Bekenstein–Hawking entropy is a quarter of the horizon area counted in Planck areas, and the Hawking temperature combines ħ, c, G and k_B; it is the clearest formula in which all four constants appear together, which is why black holes serve as a quantum-gravity laboratory.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)
Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Planck-suppressed dispersion and GRB time-of-flight bounds
summary: If quantum gravity changes photon dispersion at order E/E_P, high-energy photons from distant gamma-ray bursts arrive with energy-dependent delays proportional to E/E_P times the light-travel time; Fermi-LAT timing of GRB 090510 pushed the linear-order scale beyond E_P, so the Planck scale itself is now an experimentally probed quantity.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: Scale-free vacuum GR: one simulation serves all masses
summary: The vacuum Einstein equations have no intrinsic length scale, so binary-black-hole simulations are run in units of total mass M and rescale to any mass: times and lengths scale as GM/c^3 and GM/c^2, and strain is (GM/c^2)/D times a universal function. Matter breaks this scaling, which is why neutron-star mergers must be simulated separately for each equation of state.
map: t\to\lambda t,\ x\to\lambda x,\ M\to\lambda M:\quad f_{\rm GW}\propto\frac{c^3}{GM},\ h\propto\frac{GM}{c^2D}

name: Constancy of constants tests the equivalence principle
summary: Local position invariance, part of the Einstein equivalence principle, requires dimensionless constants such as α and m_p/m_e to be the same everywhere and at all times; atomic-clock comparisons, the Oklo natural reactor and quasar spectra bound their drift, and any variation would generically also violate the weak equivalence principle.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

name: SI second as proper time; relativistic geodesy
summary: The SI second is a proper time realized by clocks, so International Atomic Time is referred to an equipotential surface and corrected for gravitational redshift; optical clocks now resolve centimetre height differences, which turns the GR redshift into a geodesy tool and a requirement for any optical redefinition of the second.
sources: Pound & Rebka (1960). "Apparent Weight of Photons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 4, 337. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337)

name: MERA and holographic codes as discrete AdS
summary: In a tensor network, a boundary region's entropy is bounded by the number of bonds a minimal cut crosses times log χ, a discrete Ryu–Takayanagi formula; MERA's renormalization direction resembles a hyperbolic slice of AdS (Swingle), and holographic codes built from perfect tensors model bulk reconstruction as quantum error correction.
breaks: Exact RT behaviour holds only for special (stabilizer or random) networks with flat entanglement spectra; there is no sub-AdS locality or Einstein dynamics, and MERA's emergent geometry has been argued to be closer to de Sitter or light-cone than to a spatial AdS slice.
sources: Ryu & Takayanagi (2006). "Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181602. [arXiv:hep-th/0603001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0603001)

name: Machine learning for GW searches, glitches and inference
summary: Convolutional networks detect compact-binary signals and classify instrumental glitches (Gravity Spy), normalizing-flow simulation-based inference gives full posteriors in seconds, and ML surrogates of numerical-relativity waveforms speed up parameter estimation, complementing matched filtering and stochastic sampling.

name: MCMC and nested sampling for GW source parameters
summary: Posteriors over the ~15 parameters of a compact binary are sampled with Markov-chain Monte Carlo and nested sampling (LALInference, Bilby), direct descendants of the Metropolis algorithm; nested sampling also yields the Bayesian evidence used for model selection and tests of GR.
sources: Metropolis et al. (1953). "Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines". *J. Chem. Phys.* 21, 1087. [doi:10.1063/1.1699114](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1699114)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Monte Carlo over geometries: causal dynamical triangulations
summary: Causal dynamical triangulations define the gravitational path integral as a sum over causal simplicial geometries, Wick-rotated and sampled by Markov-chain Monte Carlo as in lattice field theory; simulations find a phase with an extended de Sitter-like 4D geometry whose spectral dimension runs from ~4 at large scales to ~2 at short scales.

name: Hellings–Downs correlation and Bayesian evidence in PTAs
summary: A stochastic GW background makes timing residuals correlated between pulsar pairs according to the Hellings–Downs curve; PTA collaborations weigh evidence for it with Bayes factors and frequentist statistics against common-spectrum red noise, reaching ~3–4σ significance in 2023.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

name: Standard quantum limit and squeezed light in GW detectors
summary: Interferometric GW detectors are limited by fundamental instrument noise: photon shot noise and radiation-pressure noise combine into the standard quantum limit, thermal noise follows the fluctuation–dissipation theorem, and injecting squeezed vacuum (frequency-dependent since O4) beats the shot-noise limit.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: VLBI: heterodyne receivers, maser clocks and correlators
summary: The Event Horizon Telescope is an Earth-sized interferometer: each station down-converts 1.3 mm signals with heterodyne receivers and time-stamps them with hydrogen-maser clocks, and correlators combine the recordings into visibilities whose diffraction limit resolves the ~40 μas ring; imaging is then an ill-posed inverse problem solved with regularized and Bayesian methods.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L1. [arXiv:1906.11238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11238)

name: Hole argument and the meaning of general covariance
summary: Einstein's 1913 hole argument, in which diffeomorphism-related solutions agree outside a region but differ inside it, seemed to make generally covariant field equations indeterministic; its resolution (spacetime points have no identity apart from the metric) let Einstein accept general covariance in 1915 and started the modern substantivalism–relationism debate.

name: Problem of time in canonical quantum gravity
summary: Canonical quantization of GR gives a Hamiltonian constraint (the Wheeler–DeWitt equation) with no external time, the 'frozen formalism'; loop quantum gravity and philosophy of physics both face the task of defining dynamics through relational observables and of saying what change means in a timeless theory.
